When you state the value of a quantity, write the quantity's symbol as the left-hand side of the expression.
A sentence such as "its value is" followed by an expression gives the expression a name in words only,
so the reader has no symbol to cite in the steps that follow.
Writing the symbol, an equals sign, and the expression names the quantity and gives its value together.
Give the equation its own display when later steps refer to it.

The rule holds for any quantity that later steps use:

- a gradient,
- a Hessian,
- a derivative, and
- a mean [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/functions.html#def-function).

::: {#exm-symbol-on-the-left}

## Writing the gradient with its symbol

> ❌ The gradient of $f(\vx) = x_1^2 - x_2^2$ is $\tp{(2 x_1,\ -2 x_2)}$.
>
> ✅ The gradient of $f(\vx) = x_1^2 - x_2^2$ is
>
> $$
> \gradf{f}(\vx) = \tp{\paren{2 x_1,\ -2 x_2}}.
> $$

The ✅ version supplies $\gradf{f}(\vx)$, which a later line can set equal to $\vzero_{2 \times 1}$.

:::
